title: Name job steps with the canonical step vocabulary, by reference to steps.convention

facts.note: Task text mentions job steps or the step vocabulary; a hint only, not a requirement for firing.

values: job step labels authored or edited
facts.note: Whether text names job steps (in any artifact, by any actor, in any phase) and whether a label is non-canonical needs content judgement or a new vocabulary detector.

values: this protocol's text edited where it references, enumerates or defines the canonical steps
facts.note: Fires on any edit to this protocol (planner.decomposition.canonical-steps) that touches its reference to steps.convention, even when no job-step label is assigned or changed; needs an observer that maps the edited file to this rule id, plus llm judgement of whether the edit re-enumerates or redefines the steps.

fires: Any job step is named or labelled, in any artifact, by any actor, in any phase
An existing job step label is renamed or edited
This protocol is edited in a way that touches how it references, lists or defines the canonical steps, even if no job step is labelled
doesNotFire: Text that uses words like 'define' or 'execute' as ordinary verbs and does not name job steps
Edits to steps.convention itself, which owns and may define the vocabulary

given: Job steps are being named, or this protocol's reference to the step vocabulary is being edited
when: you assign a label to a job step or change how this protocol points at the canonical steps
then: Label every job step with one of the canonical steps owned by steps.convention (Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Resolve, Conclude), taking the vocabulary by reference to steps.convention.
prefer: Use the exact canonical step names: Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Resolve, Conclude
In this protocol, point at steps.convention by reference for what the steps are and mean
avoid: Inventing synonyms or project-specific step names in place of the canonical steps
Re-enumerating or redefining the steps inside this protocol (e.g. adding its own list of step meanings, extra steps, or changed definitions); copying steps.convention content here is drift
why: steps.convention owns the step vocabulary, so one shared set of step names keeps job steps consistent; this protocol references that owner instead of copying or redefining it, because copies drift. Using a step name as a label is referencing; restating what the steps are is copying.
evidence: Every job step label is one of Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Resolve, Conclude
This protocol's text points at steps.convention and contains no own enumeration or redefinition of the steps
verifier_detail: Canonical step set (term canonical_steps, owned by steps.convention): Define/Locate/Prepare/Confirm/Execute/Monitor/Modify/Resolve/Conclude; any other job step label is a finding.

Term reference_not_restate, scoped to this protocol (planner.decomposition.canonical-steps) only: this protocol references the steps and does not re-enumerate or redefine them; it points at steps.convention by reference, and copying its content into this protocol is drift. Finding: an edit to this protocol that adds or changes step definitions or a standalone step list.
audit: statement (protocol-scoped): This protocol references those steps; it does not re-enumerate or redefine them.
term_id reference_not_restate: the protocol points at steps.convention by reference; copying its content is drift.

additions.text: Activation facts, fires and doesNotFire, including the protocol-edit trigger and exclusion of steps.convention itself and of ordinary-verb uses of step words
additions.justification: Schema requires activation; the label trigger matches the unscoped S005, and the protocol-edit trigger makes S006/S010 fire even when no job step is labelled.

additions.text: Evidence checks for canonical labels and for absence of re-enumeration/redefinition in this protocol
additions.justification: Schema requires verifier-facing evidence; restates S005 and S006 as checks.

additions.text: Clarification that using a step name as a label is referencing, while restating what the steps are is copying
additions.justification: Resolves the apparent tension between the canonical list appearing in then/prefer and the reference-not-restate constraint; adds no obligation.

additions.text: Examples of re-enumeration/redefinition (own list of step meanings, extra steps, changed definitions)
additions.justification: Makes S006 operative and concrete for the planner; illustrative of the source prohibition only.

additions.text: No split: the reference-not-restate constraint is kept operative in this rule as the 'by reference' clause of then and as avoid[1]
additions.justification: Both parts are one decision about how this protocol uses the step vocabulary; a separate convention would not be operative on its own.

trace.note: Operative constraint, scoped to this protocol.
